finding.claim: The RejectWhenRequestBodyNotSpecified option checks only `input.Request.ContentLength > 0`. Go's net/http sets ContentLength to -1 for chunked (Transfer-Encoding) requests, so an attacker can send a body to an operation that declares none and the check never fires. The body is not validated, since the spec declares no requestBody. It reaches the downstream handler unvalidated, which defeats the 'reject unspecified body' control. Impact is limited to deployments that enable this option and whose handlers read the body.
finding.source: Remote HTTP client sending a request with `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` and a body to an operation with no requestBody in the spec. Precondition: Options.RejectWhenRequestBodyNotSpecified is true.
finding.sink: The handler wrapped by Validator.Middleware (or any caller of ValidateRequest) reads the unvalidated body.

trace.note: Middleware calls ValidateRequest with the incoming request.
requestBody is nil because the spec declares none, so the body is not validated.
The rejection check uses ContentLength > 0, which is false when ContentLength == -1 (chunked), so no error is returned.
The handler runs with the unvalidated body intact.

finding.guards_checked: Looked for any other body-presence check, such as req.Body != http.NoBody or a peek read. None exists on this path. The option is off by default, so this affects only opt-in users. Also checked that security requirements and parameter validation are enforced and fail closed: a missing AuthenticationFunc returns an error, and empty or nil security falls back to the global requirements. No other reachable injection, path or SSRF sinks were found, because the library only decodes and validates and does not execute, open or fetch anything. Unbounded io.ReadAll on bodies and the documented zip-bomb caveat on ZipFileBodyDecoder were treated as generic resource-limit items and not reported.
